About.Name: Flow Field Pathfinding
About.Author: Flow Field Pathfinding
About.Comment: Top-down pathfinding for many objects at once. Add your walls, then ask which direction an object should move to reach another object. Everything heading for the same spot shares one calculation, so it stays fast with many instances.

ActionMenu: Create grid covering the whole frame
Add Fusion obstacles on one layer
ExpressionMenu: Direction from object A to object B
Direction from position A to position B
Is there a path between objects?
Is there a path between positions?

Actions.Title: Create grid: %0 x %1 cells, %2 px per cell, top-left corner at (%3, %4)
Parameters: Cell size in pixels (smaller = more precise but slower to calculate; 16 is a good start)
X of the grid's top-left corner in the frame (usually 0)
Y of the grid's top-left corner in the frame (usually 0)

Actions.Title: Create grid covering the whole frame, %0 px per cell
Parameters: Cell size in pixels (smaller = more precise but slower to calculate; 16 is a good start)

Actions.Title: Clear all obstacles from the grid
Add Fusion obstacles to the grid (all layers)
Add Fusion obstacles on layer %0 to the grid
Parameters: Layer number to scan for obstacles

Actions.Title: Add %0 to the grid as obstacles
Parameters: Objects to turn into obstacles. Their current position and size are used; add them again after they move

Actions.Title: Remove %0 from the grid's obstacles
Parameters: Objects to remove (only objects that were added with Add as obstacles)

Expressions.Title: Direction(
Parameters: Fixed value of the object that wants to move, e.g. Fixed("Enemy")
Fixed value of the object to move toward, e.g. Fixed("Player")

Direction format: 4, 8, 16 or 32 = Fusion directions (0-31, ready for Set direction); 360 = smooth angle in degrees. When there is no path, or the object has arrived, its own current direction is returned so it keeps its heading

Expressions.Title: DirectionAt(
Parameters: X position of the moving object (A)
Y position of the moving object (A)
Radius of the moving object in pixels (distance from its hotspot to its farthest edge; 0 = treat it as a point)
Direction format: 4, 8, 16 or 32 = Fusion directions (0-31, ready for Set direction); 360 = smooth angle in degrees. The result is -1 when there is no path or the object has arrived

Expressions.Title: PathDistance(
Parameters: Fixed value of the object that wants to move, e.g. Fixed("Enemy")
Fixed value of the object to move toward, e.g. Fixed("Player")

Expressions.Title: PathDistanceAt(
Parameters: Radius of the moving object in pixels (distance from its hotspot to its farthest edge; 0 = treat it as a point)

Expressions.Title: HasPath(
Parameters: Fixed value of the object that wants to move, e.g. Fixed("Enemy")
Fixed value of the object to move toward, e.g. Fixed("Player")

Expressions.Title: HasPathAt(
Parameters: Radius of the moving object in pixels (distance from its hotspot to its farthest edge; 0 = treat it as a point)

Properties.Title: Cell size (pixels)
Properties.Info: Size of one grid cell in pixels. Smaller cells follow walls more precisely but cost more to calculate. 16 works well for most games; try 8 for tight spaces.

Properties.Title: Grid width (cells, 0 = fit frame)
Properties.Info: Number of cells across the grid. Leave at 0 to cover the whole frame width.

Properties.Title: Grid height (cells, 0 = fit frame)
Properties.Info: Number of cells down the grid. Leave at 0 to cover the whole frame height.

Properties.Title: Import Fusion obstacles on start
Properties.Info: Tick to copy Fusion's own obstacle objects (backdrops set to Obstacle) into the grid when the frame starts. The Add Fusion obstacles action does the same at any time.

Properties.Title: Cells processed per frame (0 = unlimited)
Properties.Info: Limits how many cells are processed each frame when targets move, spreading the work over several frames. 0 = no limit, so answers are always up to date. Try 20000 if the game stutters.
